title: Proof
body_md: If the events \(A\coloneqq\{R\oplus S=\gamma\oplus 1\}\) and \(B\coloneqq\{S\oplus T=\delta\oplus 1\}\) both occur, then the event \(C\coloneqq\{R\oplus T=\gamma\oplus\delta\}\) occurs as well. So \(A\cap B\subseteq C\). But the reverse does not necessarily hold, since \(R=\gamma, T=\delta\) with \(S=0\) satisfies \(C\) but not \(A\cap B\). Taking the complement of both sides reverses the inclusion: \(C^{\mathrm{c}}\subseteq(A\cap B)^{\mathrm{c}}=A^{\mathrm{c}}\cup B^{\mathrm{c}}\). Then applying the union bound on probabilities yields \(\mathbb{P}(C^{\mathrm{c}})\leqslant\mathbb{P}(A^{\mathrm{c}})+\mathbb{P}(B^{\mathrm{c}})\), which is the required inequality in the statement of the lemma.

label: prop:OneDetPlayer_PerfectPlay
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:OneDetPlayer_PerfectPlay}
For every \(r,s\in\{0,1\}\), there exists a \((4,2,2)\) behavior \(P_{r,s}\) satisfying the conditions in~\eqref{eq:OneDetPlayerParityCond}. Hence, the \(5\)-cycle game can be won with certainty when \(\mathsf{A}_1\) answers according to \(A^{(1)}_X=r, A^{(1)}_Z=1\oplus s\) and the other players share one four-party no-signaling resource with the distribution \(P_{r,s}\).

title: Proposition
body_md:

For the \(5\)-cycle game, arbitrary bipartite and tripartite no-signaling resources arranged according to Svetlichny-type \(2|3\) resource partitions provide no advantage over local deterministic strategies.
